facts.detail: BDUK published the Shared Rural Network Wellbeing Survey collection on 15 January 2026.
The publication is issued by Building Digital UK.
The collection provides the Shared Rural Network Wellbeing Survey Wave 1 Findings report in HTML.
Ipsos was commissioned by BDUK in 2023 to support evaluation of the Shared Rural Network programme.
The collection describes a baseline survey of 1,285 residents of households and businesses expected to benefit from enhanced SRN mobile broadband connectivity.

facts.detail: The Wave 1 findings report was published on 15 January 2026.
Baseline fieldwork ran from 15 July to 13 September 2024 across rural communities in all four UK nations.
The survey included 1,247 residents and 38 businesses, totalling 1,285 participants.
Among participants who went online, 60% reported using mobile data at least once a day.
The report is a baseline and does not estimate SRN programme impact before the planned follow-up survey.

facts.detail: BDUK published the Mobile Supplier Additionality Research collection on 15 January 2026.
The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology commissioned FarrPoint to conduct the study.
The study investigates how the number of available mobile networks in a location relates to connectivity benefits.
The publication describes the UK market context as four mobile network operators, with consolidation expected following a merger.
The research is provided in HTML and as a 32-page PDF.

facts.detail: The research finds that most tangible rural-community benefits arise once coverage is provided by a single mobile network operator.
Moving from one operator to multiple operators provides additional benefits that are generally incremental.
Additional operators mainly contribute qualitative benefits such as resilience, emergency reliability and user choice.
The report is not an evaluation of the Shared Rural Network or operators' commercial investment.
The study reports limited reliable quantifiable evidence at local rural-site level and greater reliance on qualitative evidence.

facts.detail: The evaluation plan expects final evaluation activity and recommendations to be completed in 2028.
The timetable schedules baseline indicators for November to December 2024.
The baseline wellbeing survey is scheduled across July to December 2024.
Qualitative stakeholder interviews are scheduled for January to March 2025.
Cost-benefit and value-for-money analysis is scheduled for December 2027 to January 2028.
